result:
Solutions 1 and 3 give N, and Solution 2 gives N(N+1)/2. The two formulas agree at N = 1, where the single algebraic soliton has one pole in the upper half-plane. They differ from N = 2 onward.

Solutions 1 and 3 assume each of the N algebraic solitons contributes one upper-half-plane pole. That treats the N-soliton solution as a sum of independent single-soliton pieces. The double-Wronskian tau function for the N-th rational solution has a denominator of degree growing like N(N+1) rather than N, so the pole count is not just the number of solitons. Their argument for N is therefore not justified.

Solution 2 gives N(N+1)/2, which matches the pole count I recall from the literature on these rational solutions of the massive Thirring model. Its supporting reasoning is brief (degree N(N+1), zeros in conjugate pairs, so half lie in the upper half-plane), and I haven't re-derived the degree or the pairing from the bilinear equations. I'm relying on recall of the published result, so my confidence is moderate rather than certain.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
